reviews.text: I like it. It has full tower/hero mobility. Very fast pace with some rogue lite stuff too. If you liked the creeper world games give this one a shot. +Enemies die and leave flowing liquid blood/flesh that can be used for production. Effects enemy pathing. +Terrain damage and terraforming that effects the flowing liquid. +Everything is very responsive. +The orbital abilities are more interactive than normal. Some of them you actively aim as weapons. +The heroes perform like stick shooter heroes. There is also game mode that plays like a stick shooter +Great performance. Should work on most devices. +Several game modes that all work fine for the core game play. +Control scheme compliments commonly used actions in game play very well. +The extremely fast pace and design makes failure less discouraging. Taking the rogue lite aspects into account there is no reason to be frustrated with a bad outcome. Quickly try different difficulties or go to a different level and come back again with better tech/loadout. -Sound is just weak all around. VA is AI generated. I would turn it down or mute it entirely. The combat sounds are fine, but they are so quiet. Give em some punch. -The visual style could use something to enhance depth. It looks very flat despite being 3d. -2D art is a little rough for my taste. -The story was entirely uninteresting to me. It takes up a very small portion of the game so it doesn't bother me. -The menus are odd as well. The HUD is fine in game. -Camera. A fully orbiting camera would be nice. The game is a rarity overall. The game play is great out of the box, but the visuals/sound not so much.

Interesting premise. Game play wise it's fun. Plenty of upgrades, varied units and tactics to use. It reminds me a little of SPAZ in terms of its aesthetics. Which is a good and bad thing. I'm colourblind, so this colour palette hurts my eyes. Will update as I play more, but for the price, I think it's pretty good. The writing is absolutely abysmal though.

NOTE: The dialog is awful and the story is just as bad to include heavy use of AI for character portrait animation and voice work. I will remove this when the developer ditches these add-ons. I almost did not buy it because of it, but I enjoyed the core game play. Still conflicted about this and wouldn't be surprised if they turned away customers because of it. I'd rather no voice work and still portraits than any AI inclusion. AI sucks. [strike]Additionally, the game requires you to opt-out of data analytics versus asking to opt-in. Data collection should be off by default. The game can request to collect data, that's fine, but do not make it the default. This was not fixed as of January 21, 2025.[/strike] This was confirmed fixed as of January 25, 2025. This review will stay Not Recommended, as a product you can buy, until this addressed. Otherwise, read on. ==================== I enjoyed both the Demo and Prologue for this game, so I figured I would try being a day one buyer for once. I had a good time with this game. It's waves of hordes of enemies, a pretty flexible tower placement system, heroes with light upgrades, and plenty of mission types mixed with what appears to be procedural maps. And it gets plenty hard. Starting off the bat, you could select unwinnable missions unless you figure some micro-heavy strategy I have not. As you progress through obtaining (many) types of resources, you will power up your units into standout pieces all their own. Lots of good splits, splats, and squish noises, to boot. The only thing I wish there was more of was dynamic lighting for the explosions, gunfire, and other special effects. It has that early '00s flatness to it, but otherwise looks great. You're likely to mute the music and listen to a podcast while playing before too long, though. It looks nice, no stutters with tons of enemies on screen, and loads of features to tweak, to include fully remappable keys, UI scaling, ability to turn off bloom or camera shake, and many others. It's pretty good about that for an indie title. I specifically played the longest missions with multiple ways to generate my own units along with scores of the enemies on screen, and the game never missed a beat. For what it's worth, the stability of the game with so much going on, plus no crashes, means its a solidly built piece of programming. Seems like there is a ton of stuff to do. The dev claims you can get 10+ hours out of the main content IIRC, but there are 100s of additional maps to include hard mode for them. I think if this clicks for you, you'll enjoy it. The game is missing a "survive as long as you can" mode so far. I am kind of bummed there isn't something like that. There is a sort-of solution to this as there are certain map types with survive 5/10/15 minutes in length, which only end when you choose for them to end, after meeting the time requirement, or your base is destroyed. I played a 3.5 hours long mission (shorter, in reality, from speeding up the game). The skill tree and base mechanics are the weakest. There's too many currencies to balance out, the amount you get is tedious, even with "Hard" level rewards. And its just not engaging nor strategic. It's just a grind for grind's sake. This is the weakest element of the game, more so when the upgrades are all "more" upgrades (more damage, more health, more towers) instead of doing unique things. There are better upgrades you can get while playing from the drops you accrue, but those are psuedo-random to drop. The developer did add the ability to ban and reroll in-game drops, which aids a bit, but I never found I lost due to anything not going my way except for the earliest of time with the game when learning. Lastly, some of the achievements are either broken or are just insane levels of grind. With 30 hours of gameplay, I'm about 25% complete with the 1,000 mission achievement. If I ground out the easiest levels at a brisk 2 minute pace, I'd have to play around another 27 hours to get that last achievement. There are a few other achievements that are just time sinks, like one where you kill X amount of monsters that only spawn on the last level (at least for me), and another where you have to kill 100 of one type of monster, but they spawn once per level. And the don't spawn on every map. So if you want to get 100% achievements, either grind away or give up. There's no real "achieving" anything, IMO. As a game, overall, I recommend it. At my time of last update, it was "Mostly Positive" and that's how I feel about the title. It does a bit too much, wants too much of the players time, and uses AI. I do, however, look forward to a sequel that hopefully fixes some of these issues and adds more to a solid foundation. | ==================== Edit1: Added more background as I play further. Added statement about forced data collection. Edit2: The developer has issued the first patch fixing several bugs, adding some light visual additions, and importantly, set data analytics to opt-in versus opt-out. Thank you. Edit3: Data Analytics still defaults to On and will reset itself to On everytime you start the game. Edit4: Data Analytics is now fixed. The developer is, so far, very active with the community and providing meaningful updates within the small amount of time since the game released. Edit5: Final thoughts added.

玩法框架还是蛮不错的，RTS+局内肉鸽的塔防，有着黑科技一般的炮塔拔插能力可以无缝换位置到处支援风筝怪物，相比之下用脚走路的角色更像静态防御，炮塔才是机动部队。另外各种支援火炮机枪+塔让我想起了某潜兵游戏[spoiler] For super...抱歉走错片场了[/spoiler] 但是这个关卡奖励和养成都非常迷惑，甚至可以说非常逆天。 [b] 迷惑的关卡奖励 [/b]：看似关卡解锁单位，实际上疑似是解锁你重复游玩此关卡的单位免费使用权限，这就有点无语了，总共这么多关卡，流程还不短，重复度也不低，还要我重复游玩是几个意思？凑游戏时长的方式疑似有点太极端了。 [b] 乏味的养成节奏 [/b]：你打了好几关可能也就能给科技树点个一两下，然而科技树也没啥机制解锁可言，也就一点点体感微弱的数值提升，自己解锁的单位想随便带进某些关卡还得要花费本就吃紧的资源，这个是真的逆天，那我还是用关卡免费解锁的选项吧。然后你看着每个角色科技树里都是类似每级血量提升10%左右，然后给你拉一长串等级慢慢肝这种温水养成实在是有点难绷,而且每个单位这种属性养成还只有两到三个。如果构筑里关键等级给点机制，养成丝滑点我也有动力刷吧。 [b] 需要习惯的操作 [/b]：由于这游戏的玩法，你可以框选一片单位去集群移动调整位置，但是这游戏单位选中的反馈很弱，经常会出现你想移动英雄结果炮塔瞬移到移动点的地方，有时候点地板都无法确定自己是不是取消单位选择 [b]不太明确的关卡顺序[/b]：玩demo的时候觉得这游戏玩法还蛮有意思的，但流程似乎有点短，但是玩正式版才发现原来那些不明显的小格子才是主要关卡，这个可太蛋疼了，而且一时间也不知道从哪一关开始玩比较好，只能自己随性打了 还是非常需要打磨打磨，建议最好改一改养成体验，丰富下技能科技树以及各项机制成长，优化下关卡奖励。打一局挺久的，出来感觉几乎没提升，一两次还好，连续打几关后这种感觉实在太差了。
有些太简陋，完全没有看上去那么好玩！这种防御塔没有限制的瞬间移动机制有什么意义吗？你猜猜防御塔为什么叫做塔

[h2]一款融入肉鸽元素的即时战略塔防游戏[/h2] [h3]正式版的游戏内容要比我想象得更加丰富[/h3] 之前有幸接触过游戏的试玩，对比试玩正式版可以解锁的英雄，防御炮塔，特殊建筑，以及主动技能极其丰富，在每局游戏胜利后还可获得物资，以对其进行各方面的强化；此外游戏中还多了一个空间站（资源生产管理系统），这次游戏战役以星球展开，小格子为小支线，特殊地标为主线关，游戏可进行的战役真的是超级多 [h3]或许是做了一场关于《星河战队》的梦[/h3] 剧情以人和虫的冲突展开，如果玩家曾经看过《星河战队》这部电影，那这款游戏对他来说或许不容错过，体验过程中我能感受到这款游戏有不少致敬这部电影的地方；对于一款策略性的游戏，我对于它的剧情其实并没有抱太大希望，不过在玩到这款游戏的正式版后，我觉得剧情也是蛮有趣的，其主要角色之间的拌嘴也蛮有趣味。战役中会遇到种类繁多且满屏幕密密麻麻的虫族来供玩家杀个过瘾。本作在人物对话中用到了AI配音，这点不可否认；不过我认为作为一款以生存策略玩法为主要的游戏，这对于游戏并无伤大雅。策略游戏可以着重玩法，也可看重其剧情，配音方面只不过是游戏全部的冰山一角 目前可探索区域为以idun命名的星球，星球的特殊地标为游戏的主线关卡，小格子为支线，玩家可以随自己想法通过支线打开一条通往主线的道路。核心玩法以护送装有核武器车辆摧毁虫巢、保护深钻机、驾驶机甲收集陨石、保护开采车采集资源几种为主；主线关卡会在核心玩法的基础上进行一定的修改。不同关卡所能获得的物资不同，玩家可根据所需选择关卡，所能进行的选择足够多。主线关卡的场景设计氛围感十足，再加上种类多样的虫族，这方面的体验很不错 [h3]游戏留给玩家的动手操作空间极大[/h3] 根据虫群的攻击判定，高难度下在那种有沟壑墙壁阻挡的道路，不断调整炮塔位置，让炮塔反复横跳来拉长“虫线”，能让玩家撑的更久一些；加之可以随之移动炮塔位置来不断风筝怪物，这种留给玩家很多操作空间的地方无疑会让这款游戏更加耐玩。就算是手残玩家游戏可选择的难度为简单、中等、困难完全可以选择轻松惬意的简单难度，或从简单一步步来直至挑战困难，难度选择方面游戏制作者照顾到了玩家 [h3]当然目前游戏也有很多不足之处[/h3] 最为重要的就是对于一开始就想挑战困难难度的玩家，无疑是一种折磨。困难难度对基础战备数值的要求过高，即使操作再好，也会被数值限制。这会让想开始就直接挑战困难难度的玩家去被迫刷物资升级，加上吃紧的养成资源，更容易让玩家在蛮长刷物资的过程中磨没耐心，从而影响游戏体验。对于这点游戏的改进，我觉得要么就让资源更容易获取，要么就对数值进行大量修改，或者直接在刚进入游戏就封锁困难难度到后续再进行解锁 随机武器、强化、单向进程的爬塔...星球特殊地标关卡的肉鸽模式设计的还是很不错的。但战役局内的肉鸽元素过于薄弱，甚至形同虚设，这里其实就大大折损了游戏的策略性，我觉得这里应该进行改善。游戏中的小关卡虽然极其之多，但玩法大多就是我上面列的那几类，多打几次多少都会开始腻，再加上本就弱化的战役局内肉鸽元素，无疑会在很大程度影响游戏体验 武器攻击敌人的优先级应该进行改善，像游戏中的狙击炮台这种高伤害攻速慢的武器，攻击的优先级应该是血量更加厚实的敌人，几次游戏体验中明显感觉初期的狙击炮塔有些呆头呆脑的 游戏中炮塔单位选中反馈很弱，尤其到后面炮塔多虫群多的时候，在选中英雄或者炮塔移动的时候很容易出现失误 [h3]给游戏一点建设性的提议[/h3] 要更加着重策略性而不是让玩家去刷刷刷得材料升级装备。魔高一尺，道高一丈，我觉得有制衡的游戏更耐玩，目前游戏高难度给我感觉就是刷刷刷然后各种升级堆数值，而到后面就变成哪里亮了点哪里，不仅会让刷得过程无聊，刷到最后了也会更加无聊。回到制衡，我的想法是让战役游戏中能够使用的英雄或者炮塔种类更具多样化，让每局所能选择的英雄和炮塔种类更多，且攻击方式更加具有特色，让游戏中虫族的攻击模式也更加具有特色；例如增加器械的种类像战舰这种飞船，在地面爬行的虫子没有办法打到战舰，而特殊化的巨型化飞虫能够打到，与其相对的就是地面枪械和部分英雄打不到天上飞的巨型化飞虫，而战舰和防空炮这类武器能够打到，让打法不仅仅是靠单纯的堆数量，而是一环紧扣一环。此外战役局内的肉鸽元素也应该进行改变，改善每次获得足够资源后所进行的选择，增加游戏场景中的随机事件等，想办法从玩法策略性上面让游戏得以改变 [h3]总结[/h3] 游戏的框架很好，且融入了很多内容到里面，但目前似乎有些融入的东西并不能让游戏变得更加好玩，仍然需要继续打磨打磨

I want to like it, but there are so many new player traps. The game design seems built around you knowing what to plan for in the future but the game doesnt provide any information and there are no guard rails. Had I seen the voice acting was AI, i would not have bought the game. I dont want to support this. There is a lot to be said for the gameplay, but i will simply say its mostly luck, your loadout as far as ive played has zero relevance. You wind up relyng the the RNG gods and favor stupid tactics over valid critical ones. You can build up your space station but each thing takes up slots on a grid, so you need to upgrade your station to fit more. However you need power cells to do this. You need to place a facility to produce powercells, but if you placed one of the other structures in the wrong place your ♥♥♥♥♥♥ till a mission gives you more powercells to upgrade your spacestation to produce powercells, after the game asking you to place things down before the powercells.... this is so dumb.... Oh, but i accidently spent them on something else, well ♥♥♥♥ you. Also you cant move the facility because ♥♥♥♥ you. So you have to hope a mission will provide enough cells... This isnt the only thing that likes this, every upgrade ive made so far has felt like a mistake. Only thing that has seemed to matter at all is upgrading the very basic stuff thats free. Each mission you can choose from a list of crap, some items are unlimited and once upgraded have a greater impact than any thing else ive seen so far, the other weapons are cool but have not been of any value so far. BECAUSE i cant even afford them, as i cant produce the resources to make them or upgrade things that the game is expecting. Ive got the building to produce powercells, but cant lay it down, this is the practically the beginning of the game.... The game itself runs fine and the graphics are ok. It has this cutesy look and feel to the game but feels off. It has this edge where its hardcore but then has this weird candy glaze over everything. I will try to explain, it just seems weird. Like, theres this lady you meet at the intro of the game who works for what sounds basically like the Imperium of Man. Shes talking about ritualistic implants and basically becoming a psyker or what ever. IDK. Then your fighting off massive endless waves of bugs and it gets pretty tense, but all the characters are in a good mood and happy about life. It just feels confusing. The difficulty kind of felt all over the place, i was running hard missions that seemed easier than medium and vice versa. The hardest part was getting my units to do what theyre told or accidentally moving them around. The interaction with units needs more work, it has been a pretty annoying issue. I stopped playing just now cause i asked my self, do i want to start a new game or spend the next couple missions losing out on what is effectively the tutorial with tons of resources and time wasted. Then burden myself with the question if there is even proper balance in the game to make up for this. Not only that but how many more times will i run into similar issues. Over all i like the idea, but i have some pretty harsh feelings about some core design choices. It would not take much work to address these issues i would think. But they have really just ruined the experience for me.

AI Voice Acting 10/10 - might be the best story driven game I've ever played. The character development and juxtaposition of protagonist/antagonist put IDUN light years ahead of the dribble and drool of Baulder's Gate. We should eliminate human intervention from voice acting entirely and embrace our GPT overlords. Besides the aforementioned Oscar worthy performance of "Ham", the RTS / Tower Defense bug squashing is a fine distraction to play on my MacBook Pro during office meetings, which could use some AI interruption with all these humans in the meeting room. Where is my 3x flamethrower RNG drop when I need it!

The core gameplay loop is fun enough, but the game has some serious flaws: - The AI. A message needs to be sent loud and clear that this isn't going to be accepted by gamers. Aside from the moral issues, its just terrible. The voices and their lines are just awful and distracting. - The difficulty is all over the place. It goes from boring to impossible and back again. It starts of far too difficult and then randomly you just get overwhelmed. - The RNG element is poor game design. Simple as that. Win or lose depends on drawing the right upgrade. - The meta progression and resource system is not clearly explained and is overly complex.
Upon finishing a mission the game caused a crash to restart on my PC. Upon returning to the game, all progress was lost. Too frustrating to go back in.

I also dont get the Bad Reviews ... I mean I cant say anything about the random Lootboxes luck, because im still pretty early in the game and yea it has it very hard missions ... but for now everything is manageble ... And the thing with the annoying AI Voices ... I cant tell what people mean by that ... I mean yeah they talk alot and yeah most of it is just chitchatting ... but the voices sound nice and I wouldnt even recognize them as AI voices and I dont see them as annoying in any way ... A fun roguelight tower defense game with a lot of nuance. There are two main units you use to defend your objectives, buildings and heros. Heros behave like units in an RTS, you give them orders and they move to a location. You can't target specific things with them at this time. Buildings are placed but on most levels you can rapidly relocate them around the map as you see fit. You also have abilities that are used on a cooldown, these range from a weak auto cannon to a drop pod that deploys units. All of these tools are either selected pre-mission or you receive them or upgrades as you acquire enough resources in game, which you get primarily from objectives and destroying enemy units. The game is very fast paced, with changing unit spawns and types forcing you to rapidly relocate defenses. There are a good variety of game modes, such as defending static locations, escorting a payload and walking around in a giant mech and collecting meteors. There is a slightly confusing meta progression where you build station modules to produce resources. The interface could use some smoothing (maybe allowing you to relocate modules?). It isn't bad per say just a bit rough. Otherwise you use your generated resources to upgrade your buildings, abilities and units. Many of the controls are still rough around the edges, with unit selection and movement often getting "stuck" and refusing to deselect. On missions where you can't move buildings needing to confirm each placement is also problematic as the fast paced nature of the game can require very rapid deployment of defenses. Selecting the building you want is also slower than I would like and there is no designation for which building corresponds to which key. Overall the interface is rough but I can see it being smoothed out in time. I've had a lot of fun with the game so far and I'm looking forward to updates.

以目前的游戏内容来看，不建议任何除了钱多时间也多的闲人购买并游玩这游戏，我的游玩标准已经很宽松了，但是玩了16小时再也不想碰了，问题如下： 1、比起塔防，本作其实是幸存者外壳的RTS游戏，你的防御塔需要局外成长+局内幸存者式强化，局外成长需要建设空间站和推图产出的资源，但是局外成长不如局内随机到的优秀强化一根（比如加农炮的六管模式），更别提想要补充塔的数量也得靠幸存者机制的随机奖励，导致比起塔更依赖英雄。而且在关卡准备时你只能选择几种塔且数量有限，但是局内幸存者奖励会随机出你本来就不想用的塔，选其他奖励就非常拖节奏，根本无法很流畅的使用自己设想的构筑 2、这游戏的关卡是一个星球上以六边形紧密排列的一个个节点，有一个通过500关卡的成就，不知道关卡总数是多少，但是关卡其实完全就是推车、捡球、防守这三种模式+随机生成地形的无敌复制粘贴，模式也不影响第1条提及的携带和补充塔的问题，我觉得能有耐心打通关的那也真是神人了 3、游戏综合性能最强的塔是前期就能解锁的加农炮，但是你想玩的舒服就不能往后解锁科技，因为你解锁了后面的狙击、榴弹这些意义不明的所谓高级塔之后他们就会挤占你局内幸存者奖励的池子导致你拿到加农炮和升级的几率变低，而每局你只有三次删牌三次换牌机会，开科技太多居然是负反馈也是神人了，导致我在不小心为了刀片塔解锁到刀片之后的关卡非常难抓到加农炮，这些所谓的高级塔也许经过局内外强化会有质变，但是前中期玩家不可能有足够资源去成长，对局时间太短抽不了几次卡更别提拿到好强化。所以我建议官方要么更新回退科技树功能，要么直接让玩家在局外就排除不想要的幸存者卡，不然我建议官方把你们的塔防tag删了直接换成类幸存者更不容易欺骗消费者，毕竟幸存者也有随机策略要素。你连炮塔都抠抠索索不愿意给我我玩个球的塔防呢？ 总结，建议有这个时间的玩家直接回去玩银河破裂者看几百门炮塔压着怪海炸，那起码做到了塔防的爽。
本来还不错，可到后面玩法重复就算了还特么搞一堆负面条件还禁这禁那的，你让我不爽，那就如愿给你差评

The bad: The research takes a LOT, the game is super-grindy and some of the achievements are super-super-SUPER grindy, and this game has the single worst-written and worst-acted set of characters that I've come across in a long time. I muted them relatively quickly and even in chatboxes their insipid brainfarts made me empathize with the aliens. I dunno. There's some okay tower defense buried under the giant mound of muck, but there's a LOT of muck. Take that for the sideways-hand-wavey motion it's intended as, tipped over to the thumbs down because those characters were THAT BLOODY ANNOYING EVEN WHEN MUTED.

This game starts off as a fun horde-fighting game, but i might have made a mistake by doing too many side-missions, for of those there are MANY. The story itself is rather short and the story missions are the most unique in terms of layout and gameplay. So it seems they filled out the rest of the game by giving the player 200+ sidemissions that they can choose to do. I dont know how many i did, but the mistake was absolutely doing too many side missions, it started to get too grindy after a while and made me lose interest in the game because of it, after my now 33 hours ill probably never play it again. It is fun though, if you dont overdo it. You place turrets and a few hero characters out on the map that you can move around to help out in various ways of taking care of the horde that attacks your buildings or movable units (pending on mission type). During the missions you get XP that when you level up survivors-like style get to choose an upgrade (choose 1 of 3). At first this system is good, but the more you play the more restricted the system feels and you cant get any upgrades for this outside the missions to help you out, like at all, every mission gives you around 10 or so upgrades (maybe more) and its like that no matter the difficulty you choose, so eventually you just feel stuck in the same loop you had from the start of the game. Some of the upgrades you get from leveling up during mission is get 1 more option per level up, or more xp per kill or more xp per drill and so on, and i feel like those things shouldve been upgrades you could work towards outside of missions, but instead the system stagnates, gets stiff and non progressive. Again, i might have done too many sidemissions so this got extremely apparent for me. overall, my enjoyment score for this game is about 71% I'll probably never play the game again. Also, some missions want you to survive for 15 minutes (on hard) but by holding spacebar down you can shave that down to 7.5 min (i think it doubles speed), anyway, these missions really hammer in that the XP system was made for about 15 minutes or so of gameplay at most, post 15 the xp gain slows down so much that it takes almost 10 minutes in between each level up (again, hold spacebar to shave the time down). Even if they did patch in an upgrade system for how many choices per level you get and xp gain, ill still probably never play it again.
